headline: Central Bank of Brazil Sells $1 Billion in Reserves to Curb Real Decline
summary: The Central Bank of Brazil sold $1 billion from international reserves on Thursday as the US dollar approached 5.93 reais. The move provided temporary relief amid market concerns over fiscal policy.
why: The Central Bank of Brazil manages monetary policy and foreign exchange reserves to stabilize the Brazilian real against international currencies.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Central bank dollar reserve sales directly boost foreign exchange demand for the local currency.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Direct foreign exchange reserve intervention by the central bank injected $1 billion of USD liquidity into local FX markets.
